title: Prefill granularity and load-shedding orchestrator for FlashAttn v2/v3 kernel selection
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Background: Since integrating multiple FlashAttention variants (v2 and v3) we see intermittent latency regressions triggered during bursty prefill traffic. Root cause signals point at coarse prefill batching and global kernel handoff decisions that cause oscillation and tail latency spikes under multi-tenant load. Goal: Implement a runtime orchestrator that performs per-request prefill granularity adjustments plus load-shedding heuristics to stabilize kernel selection across v2/v3, reduce tail latency regressions, and provide an automated canary + rollback path for rollout. Scope: runtime-level orchestrator (no model changes), telemetry hooks, canary policy, automated fallbacks, and a small set of integration tests and dashboards. Out of scope: UI console changes and Dedicated capacity policy changes (will be separate work). Success metrics: p95 decode latency reduction of at least 15% under identified burst patterns, <1% increase in token cost, and no regressions on the existing stability CI for 48h of continuous load replay.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can adjust prefill granularity per-request based on request fingerprint and current GPU occupancy
Load-shedding policy triggers when kernel-choice oscillation metric exceeds configured threshold and falls back to conservative v2 kernel plan
Automated canary rollout (5% traffic) with telemetry gates: latency, error-rate, and kernel-oscillation score
Integration tests that replay historical burst traces reproduce stable behavior in local harness
Operational runbook and rollback playbook documented with exact telemetry query links
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Spike finished — implemented a micro-profiler that tags requests with small runtime fingerprints (seq_len_bucket, batch_shape_hash, tenant_load_estimate). Initial profiler code pushed to runtime/spike (PR linked below).
2025-02-18: Telemetry schema agreed with Observability team. Added kernel_oscillation_score and prefill_granularity_hint fields to trace spans. Instrumentation merged (runtime PR #12345).

2025-02-25: Canary harness prototype runs against replay traces (prod-burst-2025-01-10). Observed 22% reduction p95 in synthetic runs when using adaptive prefill hints; upstream spot regression when occupancy high — added load-shedding heuristic. Details in experiment notes.
2025-03-05: Implemented fallback clamp to force v2 selection for tenants exceeding oscillation threshold. Local QA found no functional regressions; starting 1% internal canary on staging cluster.
2025-03-12: Staging canary telemetry looks good for 48h. p95 stable, no increase in error rate. Preparing production canary plan and release notes.
decisions: Use a lightweight per-request prefill_granularity_hint rather than global scheduler rewrite to minimize risk and rollout surface
Treat FlashAttn v3 as higher-throughput but higher-sensitivity kernel — therefore default conservative selection for cold or oscillating tenants
Implement load-shedding as a graceful knob (reduce prefill window / increase microbatching) instead of dropping requests
Telemetry-driven automated rollback gate: if kernel_oscillation_score > 0.15 or p95 latency increases by >10% during canary window, rollback to v2-only policy
rollout_plan: Stage 0: unit + integration tests pass in CI (runtime + replay harness)
Stage 1: internal staging canary at 1% traffic for 48h (observe metrics)
Stage 2: gradual prod canary at 5% for 24h with automatic rollback gates
Stage 3: 25% traffic for 48h if no gates tripped, then full rollout
Rollback: immediate config toggle to enforce v2-only kernel and conservative prefill policy
notes: Trade-offs: per-request hints add additional variance to routing metadata but avoid invasive changes to scheduler. We accepted slight increase in metadata cardinality for lower rollout risk.
Follow-ups: surface per-tenant kernel recommendations in console and add a Dedicated capacity knob to opt into aggressive v3 policy.
Open questions: tuning thresholds for kernel_oscillation_score; suggestion to run a 7-day continuous replay to finalize default thresholds.
